subject: Applying promo voucher balances to open invoices — accounting treatment?
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@orchardanalytics.com>

Cc: billing@orchardanalytics.com
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Voucher balance on account — can this be applied to Nov invoice?

Hi Soojin,

We ran into a little timing issue on our end — Orchard has a remaining promotional voucher balance (see attached statement) that we'd like applied against the upcoming November invoice rather than issuing a separate credit memo.

Questions from our finance team:
- Does Redwood record a credit memo if you apply voucher balances as an invoice offset, or will you record a payment/adjustment?
- What GL accounts should we expect on your side so we can mirror it in our ledger (our auditors asked for the mapping)?

We prefer the least paperwork option if it's auditable on both sides. Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Thanks,
Ellen
Ellen Park
Finance Manager, Orchard Analytics

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Voucher balance on account — can this be applied to Nov invoice?

Hi Ellen —

Thanks for the note and the statement. Copying Marcus (Finance) and Neha (Sales Ops) to align on the recommended treatment. Quick summary of what we can do:

Option A — Apply voucher as an invoice payment/offset: we post a payment on the invoice with source = "promo voucher" and decrease A/R. No external credit memo is issued unless the customer requests one for their records. This is lower friction for the customer.

Option B — Issue a credit memo and apply that credit to the invoice: produces a visible credit memo record and reduces revenue on Redwood's side via contra revenue accounting. More paperwork but sometimes preferred by customers/auditors.

Marcus — can you confirm which approach we should use for ORC-4392 and what GL mapping we should provide to the customer? I attached a draft credit memo template in case that helps.

Ellen — if you can let us know whether Orchard prefers a formal credit memo or an invoice offset, we will proceed and provide the GL references and a short explanatory note for your auditors.

Best,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Account Lead, North America
Redwood Inference
attachments: credit_memo_template.xlsx
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Voucher balance on account — can this be applied to Nov invoice?

Soojin / Neha —

Thanks for looping me in. High-level guidance for promotional voucher balances:

- If the voucher was issued as a marketing promotion (contra-revenue), we should record the impact as contra-revenue (GL: 4002) and reduce A/R (GL: 1200) when applied. That preserves revenue recognition integrity.

- If the voucher was issued as a prepaid credit (liability), then applying it is a reduction of deferred revenue/liability (GL: 2100) vs A/R.

For Orchard (based on history) I believe these were promotional rebates tied to a campaign, so my preference is to record a journal entry that debits 4002 (contra-revenue) and credits 1200 A/R, with a memo referencing voucher id and invoice number.

If the customer specifically requires a credit memo document on their account statements, we can generate one (preferred for audit trails). Otherwise, an invoice offset + internal journal is acceptable provided we share the GL mappings and a 1-page explanation for their auditors.

I've attached a sample journal entry text block we can use. I'll approve the invoice offset approach if Neha confirms this won't affect downstream commission/quotas tracking.

Marcus
Director, Finance Ops
Redwood Inference
attachments: journal_entry_example.txt
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Voucher balance on account — can this be applied to Nov invoice?

Quick note: commission is already baked into the ARR calculation for ORC-4392 and we track realized revenue on invoiced dollars. Applying the voucher as an invoice offset should not retroactively change any paid commission calculations because it's an account-level promo applied at invoicing; sales ops flags the deal as "promo-adjusted".

From a cadence perspective, customer experience team prefers to avoid extra docs unless the auditor insists. Recommend proceeding with the invoice offset and providing the one-page explanation and GL mapping to Orchard.

Neha
Senior Sales Ops Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@orchardanalytics.com>
Cc: billing@orchardanalytics.com, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Voucher balance on account — can this be applied to Nov invoice?

Hi Ellen —

Thanks for your patience. Quick update and proposed plan:

1) Redwood will apply the remaining voucher balance as a payment/offset to your November invoice (invoice #2026-11-ORC-01). This avoids producing a separate credit memo document unless you request one.

2) Internally, Redwood Finance will post a journal entry to reflect contra-revenue treatment: debit GL 4002 (contra-revenue) and credit GL 1200 (Accounts Receivable).

3) We'll provide Orchard with:
   - A short one-page note explaining the accounting treatment for auditors (attached)
   - The GL mappings (4002 / 1200) and invoice reference

If Orchard requires a formal credit memo instead, let us know and we will issue it and attach it to the account. Otherwise we'll proceed with the offset on the 11/15 invoice run.

I've attached a draft credit notice for your records; happy to revise language if your auditors need more detail.

Please confirm which you'd prefer and we'll move forward.

Best,
Soojin

Ellen
